rv.q: The show, on the other hand, doesn’t linger long in the mind.
Regardless of these book-related quibbles, this is an excellent production firing on all cylinders.

But for most of an overlong evening, the songs merely reiterate things we already know, not so much advancing the action as restating the obvious via one too many power ballads that may come across better out of context where they don’t slow down proceedings yet further.
It's a little cheesy, a little heart-rending, a little bit spectacular, but always fun.

cn.t: This cult musical about Depression-era outlaws receives a mixed West End reception, with critics divided on its relentless pacing and romantic treatment of killers, though Frances Mayli McCann's performance earns widespread praise.
